title: Proof of knowledge
intro: In cryptography, a proof of knowledge is an interactive proof in which the prover succeeds in 'convincing' a verifier that the prover knows something. What it means for a machine to 'know something' is defined in terms of computation.

title: Proof of secure erasure
intro: In computer security, proof of secure erasure (PoSE) or proof of erasure is a remote attestation protocol, by which an embedded device proves to a verifying party, that it has just erased (overwritten) all its writable memory. The purpose is to make sure that no malware remains in the device.

title: Proof of space
intro: Proof of space (PoS) is a type of consensus algorithm achieved by demonstrating one's legitimate interest in a service (such as sending an email) by allocating a non-trivial amount of memory or disk space to solve a challenge presented by the service provider. The concept was formulated in 2013 by Dziembowski et al.

title: Proof of stake
intro: Proof-of-stake (PoS) protocols are a class of consensus mechanisms for blockchains that work by selecting validators in proportion to their quantity of holdings in the associated cryptocurrency. This is done to avoid the computational cost of proof-of-work (PoW) schemes.

title: Proof of the Euler product formula for the Riemann zeta function
resolved_title: Proof of the Euler product formula for the Riemann zeta function
intro: Leonhard Euler proved the Euler product formula for the Riemann zeta function in his thesis Variae observationes circa series infinitas (Various Observations about Infinite Series), published by St Petersburg Academy in 1737.

title: Proof of work
intro: Proof of work (also written as proof-of-work, and abbreviated PoW) is a form of cryptographic proof in which one party (the prover) proves to others (the verifiers) that a certain amount of a specific computational effort has been expended. Verifiers can subsequently confirm this expenditure with minimal effort on their part.

title: Proof procedure
intro: In logic, and in particular proof theory, a proof procedure for a given logic is a systematic method for producing proofs in some proof calculus of (provable) statements.

title: Proof sketch for Gödel's first incompleteness theorem
resolved_title: Proof sketch for Gödel's first incompleteness theorem
intro: This article gives a sketch of a proof of the first of Gödel's incompleteness theorems. This theorem applies to any formal theory that satisfies certain technical hypotheses, which are discussed as needed during the sketch.

title: Proof test
intro: A proof test is a form of stress test to demonstrate the fitness of a load-bearing or impact-experiencing structure.  An individual proof test may apply only to the unit tested, or to its design in general for mass-produced items.

title: Proof that 22/7 exceeds π
intro: Proofs of the mathematical result that the rational number ⁠22/7⁠ is greater than π (pi) date back to antiquity. One of these proofs, more recently developed but requiring only elementary techniques from calculus, has attracted attention in modern mathematics due to its mathematical elegance and its connections to the theory of Diophantine approximations.
